<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|56|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XX.}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XX.}}}}}}

{{c|''To shew how through Gods grace the Iewes shalbe ouerrunne of the Gentils, although they beginne after, he bringeth a parable of men working soner and later in the vineyard, but the later revvarded in the end euen as the first. 17 He reuealeth more to his Disciples touching his passion: 20 Bidding the ambitious two suiters to thinke rather of suffering with him: 24 And teaching vs (in the rest of his Disciples) not to be greeued at our Ecclesiastical Superiors, considering they are (as he was him self) to toile for our Saluation. 29 Then going out of Iericho, he geueth sight vnto tvvo blind.''}} {{verse|chapter=20|verse=1}}THE {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpon the Sunday of Septuagesme.}}kingdom of heauen is like to a man that is an housholder vvhich vvēt forth early ‖ in the morning to hire vvorkemen into his vineyard. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=2}}† And hauing made couenāt vvith the Workemen for a penie a day, he sent them into his vineyard. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=3}}† And going forth about the third houre, he savv other standing in the market place idle, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=4}}† and he said to them, Goe you also into the vineyard: and that vvhich shal be iust, I vvil giue you. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=5}}† And they vvent their vvay. And againe he vvent forth about the sixt & the ninth houre: and did likevvise. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=6}}† But about the eleuenth houre he vvent forth and found other standing, & he saith to them, What stand you here al the day idle? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=7}}† They say to him, Because no man hath hired vs. He saith to them, Goe you also into the vineyard.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=8}}† And vvhen euening vvas come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his bailife, Call the vvorkemen, and pay them their hire, beginning from the last euen to the first. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=9}}† Therfore vvhen they vvere come that came about the eleuenth houre, they receiued euery one a ‖ penie. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=10}}† But vvhen the first also came, they thought that they should receiue more: and they also receiued euery one a penie. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=11}}† And receiuing it they {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Iewes are noted for enuying the vocation of the Gentiles, and their reward equal with thē selues.}}∷ murmured against the good man of the house, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=12}}† saying, These last haue continued one houre: and thou hast made them equal to vs that haue borne the burden of the day and the heates. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=13}}† But he ansvvering said to one of them, Frende, I doe the no vvrong: didst thou not couenant vvith me for a penie? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=14}}† Take that is thine, and goe: I vvil also giue to this last euen as to thee also. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=15}}† Or, is it not lavvful for me to do that I vvil? is thine eye naught, because I am good? {{verse|chapter=20|verse=16}}† So shal the last, be first: and the first, last. For many be called, but ‖ fevv elect.⊣

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 10, 32. Luc. 18, 31.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in a votiue Masse of the holy Crosse.}}And IESVS going vp to Hierusalem, tooke the tvvelue disciples secretly, and said to them, {{verse|chapter=20|verse=18}}† Behold vve goe vp to<noinclude>{{rh|||Hierusalem,}}</noinclude>
